title: First side of the product graph under proper ambient change
statement: Fix schemes $X,Y$, a morphism $f:X\to Y$, a compactification $c$, two proper/open/proper presentations $s,t$ [def-pur-etale-graph-presentation-maps], and a finite commutative ring $A$. Suppose $pr:P_t\to P_s$ is proper and $q:U_t\to U_s$ makes the open square Cartesian, with $a_tq=a_s$ and $pr p_s=p_t$. Let $D_1$ be the explicit first-neighborhood transport of [def-pur-etale-graph-proper-ambient-data]. The first graph-side maps $B_{1,s},B_{1,t}$ of [lem-sf-etale-locally-closed-graph-model] satisfy $B_{1,s}D_1=B_{1,t}$ as natural transformations. No statement about the intersection word or second side is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose) and 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal); applied to the explicit product-graph formula.

proof.text: Use the explicit product and neighborhood maps, their Cartesian squares, and their graph and projection equations.

Factor the first side as the common identity insertion followed by proper ambient transport. Apply the transport composition law to the old side and the first-neighborhood transport. Both projection equations identify the resulting rectangle with the new side square. The common identity insertion gives exactly the first-side equation.

proof_origin.place: Proper-projection grids of the graph construction, vertical and horizontal pasting, Tags 0F7C--0F7D.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleGraphProperAmbientFirstSide
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (c : Compactification f)
    (s t : EtaleGraphPresentation f) (pr : t.P ⟶ s.P) [IsProper pr]
    (q : t.U ⟶ s.U) (sq : IsPullback q t.e s.e pr)
    (hz : t.a ≫ q = s.a) (hp : pr ≫ s.p = t.p) :
    (locallyClosedGraphSide₁ s.a s.e s.p c.i c.g
      ((Category.assoc _ _ _).trans (s.fac.trans c.comm)) A).hom ≫
        (s.properAmbientFirstTransport c t pr q sq hz hp A).hom =
      (locallyClosedGraphSide₁ t.a t.e t.p c.i c.g
      ((Category.assoc _ _ _).trans (t.fac.trans c.comm)) A).hom
